Highlight Clip: CZ: The Real Demand for Tokenized US Stocks Comes from Outside the US CZ: The Real Demand for Tokenized US Stocks Comes from Outside the US On October 27, 2026, Binance founder CZ said in an interview with The Rollup founder Andy that demand for tokenized U.S. stocks primarily comes from people outside the United States who struggle to open U.S. brokerage accounts. He noted that in some countries with populations exceeding 100 million, the entire stock market’s daily trading volume is just $50 million, comparable to the volume handled by a single trader in New York. He believes companies in these markets could tokenize their shares to reach global investors and enable round-the-clock trading. Tokenization could also extend to assets that lack established trading venues, such as water, rare earth minerals and certain precious metals, providing them with trading access and liquidity. — link

Bithumb Details Internal System Breach: 6,444 Customers and 715 Employees Compromised South Korea's second-largest crypto exchange, Bithumb, disclosed that an unauthorized external intrusion into its internal corporate groupware (DaouOffice) for approximately one hour on October 27 resulted in the exfiltration of personal data belonging to 6,444 customers. The compromised records include names, mobile numbers, resident registration numbers, bank account numbers, and copies of identification documents—of which 5,600 records remained encrypted and unreadable, while data belonging to 844 customers was directly exposed, alongside records of 715 employees and external personnel. Bithumb emphasized that the breached groupware is completely isolated from its core trading operations and asset databases, ensuring that customer funds remain secure, while noting it has formally notified authorities and pledged full compensation for any verified damages resulting from the incident. — link

NYSE Parent ICE Plans to Partner With Trade xyz to Launch Perpetual Futures Market in the US According to Bloomberg, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is partnering with Trade xyz to launch regulated perpetual futures contracts in the United States. The planned venue is slated to run on Hyperliquid's infrastructure with dedicated clearing, KYC, and AML compliance frameworks, featuring products pegged to equities, indexes, commodities, and FX pending regulatory approval. As part of the collaboration, ICE will take an equity stake in Trade xyz under undisclosed terms. Trade xyz has previously rolled out perpetual contracts tied to traditional assets like crude oil and equity benchmarks on Hyperliquid. — link

Russian Central Bank: Restrictions on Non-Custodial Wallets Do Not Apply to Cross-Border Settlements According to TASS, Vladimir Chistyukhin, First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Russia, stated that proposed restrictions on non-custodial crypto wallets under the draft legislation regulating cryptocurrency circulation will not apply to international settlements, where the use of non-custodial wallets will remain permitted. Chistyukhin noted that while allowing domestic Russian investors to utilize non-custodial wallets was initially considered during the drafting process, authorities ultimately decided against permitting direct investments via non-custodial wallets due to investor protection concerns, AML requirements, and oversight constraints. However, the forthcoming restrictions do not prevent users from transferring cryptocurrencies from domestic custodial wallets to foreign custodial wallets, and subsequently moving them into non-custodial wallets. — link
